The huge wind farms have a number of issues, not the least of which being that every wind farm only ever runs at between 1/2 and 2/3 capacity, tops.

The first major issue is that when the government started subsidizing it (to the tune of billions of dollars), lots of people formed corporations, got government grants, and then went to various European companies and bought their decommissioned first- and second-generation equipment that was originally manufactured in the late 80s or early 90s. So, the US taxpayer shelled out top dollar for wind power equipment and ended up with garage-sale-tiered garbage.

The second issue is that those huge windmills have a lot to them, and require lots of expensive, regular maintenance. They run X number of hours, and then all the internals get tore out and replaced, then sent out for repair. A lot of people don't realize, but one example is this: Those things don't just run when the wind blows. Because of their size, they have to be kept moving, so inside each one is a giant battery bank and a series of drives and motors that keep the blades spinning at a certain RPM. Also, each windmill only generates clean, usable power when the blades spin the turbines at that same certain RPM, so each blade has a drive and a motor to adjust the angle of the blade so that if the wind is blowing harder, it takes less of a "cut" (sorry, don't know the proper term) through the air and doesn't spin too fast; likewise, when the wind isn't blowing as hard, the blades adjust for more of a "cut", so that less wind will spin them as much as they need to spin to generate good power. All those drives and motors and the PLCs that control them and the gearboxes and other mechanical parts have to be rebuilt after X number of hours, not including their failure rate from overheating or overload or being hit by lightning or whatever else happens to them.

This all costs incredible amounts of money.
